statement: The 40 Hour Famine was described as a fundraising scheme in which Australians, especially young people, went without food for 40 hours and sought sponsorship from others.

overlays.overlay_statement: Fundraising uses a participant-led sponsorship challenge in which individuals undertake a voluntary deprivation activity and solicit pledges from their networks.
overlays.why_adds_value_beyond_canonical: Identifies the reusable fundraising mechanism and participant role.
overlays.anti_duplication_boundary: Excludes event branding, dates, amounts and ordinary participant demographics.
overlays.qualification: The deprivation activity is represented as a fundraising device, not as a service or beneficiary intervention.

overlays.overlay_statement: Young people can participate as active fundraisers and network mobilisers rather than only as donors.
overlays.why_adds_value_beyond_canonical: Adds a participation distinction concerning who performs the fundraising activity and how.
overlays.anti_duplication_boundary: Does not duplicate the sponsorship mechanism; focuses on participant agency.
overlays.qualification: Apply where youth participation is materially part of the described scheme.
